opencode.note: OpenCode v2 never auto-updates under OLYMPUS. The vendored CLI is updated only after the isolated conformance gate approves the exact version; 2.4.1 passed the full gate on 2026-11-23.

releases.title: Hygiene total — zero errors
highlights: npm run hygiene is the gate of record: tsc, lint, docs, privacy, suite manifest and audit-high all pass; add --battery for the 54 hermetic suites.
HYGIENE.md declares the zero-error contract and every remaining limit (23 moderate transitive advisories, local suites, drills not claimed).
The 0.0.98 preview releases are retired from Releases (tags kept); v0.0.98 is the base and v0.0.99 is the current stable.
The 0.0.98 line is complete: generation boundary, Portfolio, delivery profiles, Plan Health, Recovery Log/real errors, OpenCode 2.4.1, boot truth, slow-lane truth and the verification guard.
No external projects were created; AIME remains the active development lane.

releases.title: The walk waits, recovers and reports — and the Logs tell the truth
highlights: The GO 5-hour limit is now a WAIT, not an unknown stop: provider.go-limit/quota maps to provider-quota, the walk pauses and resumes at the console reset. The old overnight park (21:31 → 06:25) can no longer burn a night.

A blocked design gate recovers its quarantined dependencies (the real QA parks), not the gate. The end-of-walk report is deterministic and always written; the digest now counts the hop state (6/10, not 4/10).
Apollo's chat gets a durable campaign reporter: hop green/parked, quota wait and the final report are in the inbox, so a detached walk still speaks after a reload.

New Logs workspace: Visão geral, Hops, Walks, Models and Economy, with full hop/walk detail — god, build, model, declared abilities, artifacts, checks, park, recovery, resonance, tokens, step cost/list/invoice.

The terminal header now carries the GO limit meter: 5h by default, one button toggles weekly/monthly; stale anchor and quota-hit are labelled. The meter reads the console anchor only (no 57k ledger scan).
Hibernation now opts the active lane in and starts the detached walk, so the night contract survives the renderer being destroyed.
The qwen3.7-plus guard and the exact console windows from v0.0.97 remain. OpenCode v2 2.3.2 remains the latest npm release and gate-approved.

The task sheet now shows the build's own loadout (skills/MCPs/demigods even when the hop declares none), lane health, live tool counts, the last park/recovery and the settled output tail — no more 0/0 with no explanation.
Learning notifications are live and clickable: the box shows the teaching, measured confidence/samples and exactly how far it is from the 85% short-circuit gate, with the last outcomes.
Callimachus gets a brain-health card (seed/empirical, average confidence, short-circuit rate, the 85% gate) and a 'curar agora' action; his reference shelf now includes the vault knowledge docs.

Pattern Studio: moving the pointer attracts the particle field, clicking the background pulses it, and clicking a thought opens its analysis box (what it is, connections, associated learning) — the learning rows open the same detail.
Boot: one full-screen loader loops until every mounted panel is loadable, instead of a stack of per-panel loaders; the brain's focus card no longer covers the live logo.
The Logs hop detail now shows the output tail and falls back to the frozen plan for historical hop definitions; the hop table is a responsive two-line list with cost visible.

releases.title: The GO console is the anchor — no more stale burn
highlights: The logged-in OpenCode GO console is already an OLYMPUS frame; every 30s it is parsed (monthly / rolling / weekly + reset) and posted as the anchor, source browser. The app graph follows 46% / 100% / 52% with no manual copy.

A console anchor older than 5 minutes PAUSES upgrades. Rolling ≥65% steps down, ≥80% enforces Reserve, and 100% is a quota-hit: the walker parks with the console reset time and Burn/Pace are disabled.
The burn panel shows the console anchor age, the rolling number, the stale/quota banners and the resume time; off/reserve remain available.

The interactive chat now pins the session model to the current god's model every message. The unverified GO qwen3.7-plus lane falls back to verified DeepSeek, so a qwen turn can no longer leave Apollo riding the same dead lane.

Verified live: the console frame auto-synced 46% monthly / 100% rolling / 52% weekly and the quota guard parked the walk; after the rolling window reset the frame reported 0% rolling, then 47% monthly / 1% rolling / 52% weekly as the first post-reset turn landed, and the guard released. The qwen guard maps to opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash.
OpenCode v2 2.3.2 remains the latest npm release and gate-approved.

releases.title: Hibernation v2, GO truth and the smart burn
highlights: X now quits by default; hibernate is explicit (tray, lock, or the close-to-hibernate preference). A real quit stops the preview/MCP fleet instead of leaving it in the app cgroup.
Hibernate waits for a streaming chat turn, keeps a preview only when a live hop needs it, records the servers it stops, and the wake restores them automatically.
The hibernation HUD has a collapse button: 420×720 → 340×190 (campaign, GO month, in-flight hop only); expand restores the full widget.
The GO graph uses the console anchor (monthly/5h/weekly) plus the local delta; the weekly window resets Monday 00:00 UTC. The measured 25.1% / 50.1% matches the console's 25% / on-pace-50%.

Smart burn chooses a GO-only roster at the next hop/message (Kimi K3, Kimi K2.7 Code, DeepSeek 1017, Qwen3.7 Plus, MiniMax M3). Claude Opus/Sonnet are Zen models, not in the GO catalog; the screen says so instead of guessing.
The burn toggle never rewrites opencode.json and never cuts a live turn; it applies at the hop/message boundary and diversifies top lanes so one per-model cap cannot carry all ten gods.
OpenCode v2 2.3.2 remains the latest npm release and is gate-approved; the patch-notes screen checks the live latest on every open.
A tag-icon/logo audit and a 24px vector brief are in docs/design/TAG-ICON-BRIEF.md; the 16px marks are hand-authored, not model-generated.
Wake ignores ERR_ABORTED (the splash → APP_URL navigation) instead of entering a reload loop; the preview restore probes and retries until verified.
Max Quality / strategy apply resolves the real app root in standalone (not .next/standalone); the L4 probe falls back to the package binary. Verified ok:true.

releases.title: OpenCode 2.3.2 alignment and the patch-notes screen
highlights: OpenCode v2 2.3.2 passed the isolated conformance gate (serve, v2 sessions, prompt/SSE, DB schema, tokens, abort) and a real Apollo turn.
The boot loader now shows a What's new card after the first second; a hibernate return repaints the same loader, so the alignment is visible during a slow wake.
A status-bar Patch notes button opens the full updates screen from anywhere; /patch-notes is also a standalone page.
The screen reads the installed and npm-latest OpenCode versions live and takes the tested version from patch-notes.json, so it stays updatable without hardcoding the UI.
The update lane still refuses an ungated version and shows the conformance command instead of updating blind.

releases.title: The preview that obeys, the marks that cannot be lost
highlights: Browser previews keep 127.0.0.1 (the project session survives); Electron alone uses the isolated 127.0.0.2 OOPIF origin for 60 FPS.
Apollo mark batches are durable background plans with plan/latest/retry, a 20-minute budget and boot-aware stale recovery.
The small preview sends to Apollo; every non-quick mark is saved to the project queue before the turn.
Hibernation stops managed dev servers and prunes an expired window; dev servers report RSS, adopt the true port owner and restart in place.
Next.js 16.4.6 closes the advisory that made 16.4.2 fail the build.

releases.title: Performance: the preview gets its own renderer
highlights: Electron runs the live preview as an OOPIF on 127.0.0.2; AIME measured parent 54 → 60 FPS and iframe 52 → 60 FPS.
GPU is on by default; a persisted software-rendering marker was retired.
Progressive boot waits for the shell, not nine panel endpoints; heavy panes show their own branded loaders.
